name: Sugar Vinegar
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: the best white sugar
ingredients.originalText: 1 pound of the best white sugar

ingredients.name: 1 jill or more of strong yeast
ingredients.originalText: 1 jill or more of strong yeast
ingredients.quantityText: 1 jill or more of strong yeast

instructions.text: To every gallon of water allow a pound of the best white sugar, and a jill or more of strong yeast
Mix the sugar and water together
Boil and skim it till the scum ceases to rise
When it cools to lukewarm heat, put into it the yeast spread on pieces of toast
Put it into an iron-hooped cask
Set it in a sunny place for five months, leaving the bung loose, but keeping the bung-hole covered
In five months it will be good clear vinegar

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. To every gallon of water allow a pound of the best white sugar, and a jill or more of strong yeast
2. Mix the sugar and water together
3. Boil and skim it till the scum ceases to rise
4. Pour it into a tub
5. When it cools to lukewarm heat, put into it the yeast spread on pieces of toast
6. Let it work two days
7. Put it into an iron-hooped cask
8. Set it in a sunny place for five months, leaving the bung loose, but keeping the bung-hole covered
9. In five months it will be good clear vinegar
10. Bottle it for use
